title: The Ceiling on a Credit Posted to a Rider Premium Account
content:
Every credit posted against a rider premium charge on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is bounded by a ceiling, and the ceiling is settled by the standing of the rider.

## The rule

1. Where the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium, the ceiling is the whole of the charge being put right, the whole of it standing to be relieved while the premium is owed.
2. Where the rider record carries a day the rider ended, nothing further is credited, what was owed having been settled when the rider was closed.
3. Otherwise, the ceiling is the charge being put right less the credits already posted to the rider premium account, and is never less than nothing.

## Condition and ceiling

| The rider's standing | The ceiling |
|---|---|
| Suspended for unpaid premium | The whole of the charge being put right |
| Carrying a day the rider ended | Nothing further |
| Any other standing | The charge being put right, less the credits already posted, never less than nothing |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Take a charge being put right of 57.20 USD, with credits already posted to the rider premium account coming to 40.00 USD.

- **Suspended for unpaid premium:** the ceiling is the whole 57.20 USD, the credits already posted not being taken off it.
- **The record carrying a day the rider ended:** the ceiling is nothing, and nothing further is credited.
- **Any other standing:** the ceiling is 57.20 USD less 40.00 USD, that is 17.20 USD.

Where the credits already posted came to 60.00 USD in that third case, the ceiling would be nothing rather than a negative figure, being never less than nothing.
